_why: PERF PREMISE WITHDRAWN 2026-09-16 — this is a CORRECTNESS issue only. A profile of test_stream_table_join_baseline_performance at 200k records (117,697 samples, 96.7% of self-time symbolised) puts merge_join_records_with_aliases and all three combine_records_with_nulls* at 0.00% INCLUSIVE. They do not execute in that workload; q3's stream-table route runs JoinOperator::execute_take_path and never enters JoinProcessor. The original framing — 'per-record join paths' where the map costs N hashes plus a bucket allocation per record — is not supported by measurement, and any claim of a speedup must not be made. What the profile DOES show, for the record and NOT as scope here: JoinLayout 4.60% inclusive (its own name_pos map in shadow_or_append 2.14%) — NOTE: an earlier revision said 10.52%, which was inflated by double counting: the script summed every matching symbol per stack, so a stack containing both from_sides and append_relation counted twice. Corrected by counting each sample ONCE per pattern, arrow_schema::Fields::find 2.29% (by-name lookup on a hot path), ~30% of self-time in allocator/memmove/memset, and — the actual hot path — take_combine_stream_table at 29.99%, which rebuilds BOTH field-name Vec<Arc<str>> (one allocation per column per call) AND the whole JoinLayout on every call, from inputs that are stable for a query (hash_join.rs:392-415). The existing OnceLock/RwLock cache covers the output SCHEMA, not the layout that derives it. That is plan-time work on the hot path and is the real lever; it also explains why the shadow_or_append micro-fix measured nothing. A linear-scan replacement for shadow_or_append's map was tried and MEASURED at 2.19% vs 2.17% — no gain, and quadratic at high column counts — so it was reverted. Those are architectural, not local. THE CORRECTNESS DEFECT IS UNCHANGED AND REAL: four join record-construction sites build an ORDERED JoinLayout and then pour it into an FxHashMap, letting hash iteration decide the emitted column order. Two carry docs promising a specific physical layout. from_explicit's own contract says 'Pass a Vec (not FxHashMap) at call sites where column order is meaningful' — these sites have a schema (layout.entries() IS it) and discard it. None is broken today: they agree because FxHash is seed-free and all four share a key set, so the order is stable BY ACCIDENT. That accident already broke once — columnar/adapter.rs::batch_to_records had the identical defect, its doc promising schema order while a map decided it, and #1918's EXPR$<n> -> EXPR_<n> rename perturbed the hashes and surfaced it. It was found by an ad-hoc flake probe, NOT by the 11,797-test suite. These four are the same latent defect awaiting the next rename. #2121 already generified project_into over IntoIterator, which was the signature forcing callers to erase order, so this is now a per-site change with no API work.

acceptance: The FOUR in-scope join.rs sites pass a LAZY ITERATOR to project_into / from_explicit — no intermediate FxHashMap and no intermediate Vec. build_batch (stream_record/mod.rs) consumes impl IntoIterator in a single for loop and sizes its Vecs from a fixed TYPICAL_DATA_COLS hint, never from the input's length, so it needs neither len() nor a second pass. Before: N hash computations plus a bucket allocation per record, for a map whose only purpose is to be iterated once and dropped. A Vec would still pay one allocation. The lazy iterator saves the map's N hashes and its bucket allocation — but NOT all allocation: build_batch (stream_record/mod.rs:357-367) always allocates three Vecs from a fixed const TYPICAL_DATA_COLS = 4 hint, never from the input, and a two-relation join layout routinely exceeds 4 data columns, so the lazy form still pays reallocs inside build_batch. An earlier draft said 'pays none', which the microbench this spec mandates would have contradicted. The direction of the result is unaffected: the map form pays those same reallocs on top of the hashing.

The four sites are at origin/master join.rs lines 651, 712, 933 and 965 (symbol anchor: 'for entry in layout.entries()', 5 occurrences; re-measured at ce56ad5be — an earlier draft of this spec carried 650/711/922/954/1382, read from a stale origin/master in another worktree). Line 1393 is the FIFTH occurrence and is NOT in scope: it iterates layout.entries() to compute column INDICES, not to build a field map. Leave it untouched and say so in the report.
Emitted column order equals layout.entries() order BY CONSTRUCTION at all four sites, not by hash accident.

A fail_to_pass test proves the defect is observable: join_emits_columns_in_layout_order_under_adverse_hash_order constructs a join whose column NAMES hash such that FxHashMap iteration order differs from layout order, and asserts the emitted record's column order matches the layout. It must FAIL at the pinned base ce56ad5be (hash order wins) and pass after. PINNED LOCATION: create tests/unit/sql/execution/processors/join/join_layout_order_test.rs and register it in that directory's mod.rs as 'pub mod join_layout_order_test;' with a '// #2138:' comment, matching the convention every other entry there follows. Registration is not optional bookkeeping — an unregistered test file is never compiled, so it cannot fail, and the §7a baseline run would record a RED-FIRST line for an assertion that never executed. Copy BOTH the file and the mod.rs edit into the baseline worktree. This is the whole proof that the defect is real rather than theoretical — the class was previously only ever surfaced by accident.

The columnar byte-parity suite stays green — parity_multi_col_key and parity_computed_key in particular. They compare columns POSITIONALLY (assert_eq! on a Vec of column names), which makes them the canary for any ordering change.
New tests are registered in the parent mod.rs

URGENCY, stated so nobody over-reads this issue: three of the four sites fire only on unmatched rows in outer joins, so the per-record cost lands on outer-join misses rather than on every joined record. The earlier framing 'all four are per-record join paths' is true but misleading. The CORRECTNESS half — hash order deciding emitted column order where a doc promises a layout — applies to all four equally and is the reason this issue exists.

Each of the four sites is converted in its OWN commit, with cargo check --no-default-features --tests passing before the next begins. Four commits each touching one site is the audit trail, and unlike a rule about editing technique it is visible in git history — agent.log is gitignored, so evidence that lives only there is not auditable by a reviewer reading the PR. NOTE: this bar and the pack_join_results order-stability bar are deliberate SPEC ADDITIONS that go beyond the issue text (the issue asks only for 'ast-grep per shape, or four targeted edits'). They are kept because a regex rewrite during #1918 deleted one of these very four functions, and because every other bar is scoped at the four sites while the defect is observable at query level. Recorded as additions so neither is mistaken for optional.

The constructor docs are updated to match the pinned design, quoted accurately. from_explicit (stream_record/builder.rs:859-863) says the iteration order 'is the schema-declared column order for the resulting record. Pass a `Vec` (not `FxHashMap`) at call sites where column order is meaningful (index-based dispatch, #383)', and project_into (builder.rs:150-151) says 'Pass a `Vec` where column order is meaningful; an `FxHashMap` remains valid for genuinely schemaless merges.' After this change the preferred form is a LAZY ORDERED ITERATOR, which allocates nothing, with a Vec merely acceptable — reword both to say so, keeping FxHashMap valid for genuinely schemaless merges. Include from_explicit_with_key (builder.rs:896), which is what site 651 ACTUALLY calls and so is the constructor a reader lands on from that site; it is already generic over IntoIterator and carries no ordering claim, so nothing false ships if skipped, but it would be the one door into this code left without the reworded contract. Leaving these as-is would ship a contract telling the next caller to allocate — the doc-contradicts-code defect this whole chain exists to remove. MARKED AS A SPEC ADDITION: the issue text does not ask for the doc rewording. It is kept because shipping the pinned design while the docs still tell the next caller to allocate is the doc-contradicts-code defect this chain exists to remove. Flagged so it is not mistaken for optional, alongside the four-commit rule and the pack_join_results bar.

EVERY REACHABLE site gets a behavioural assertion — reporting is the fallback for unreachable ones only. A test constructing 'a join' can prove one route while leaving combine_records_with_nulls_for_probe (batch probe NULL) and combine_records_with_nulls_for_right_join (RIGHT-join NULL-left) untouched, so name which site each assertion drives. A site may be left unasserted ONLY if no public execution path reaches it, and then the reachability bar's evidence is what justifies it. Note the two pass_to_stay canaries cannot substitute: both are GROUP BY shapes that never route through JoinProcessor, so they guard against a regression elsewhere, not coverage here. This issue exists because a defect of exactly this class sat unnoticed behind tests covering a sibling path — 'covered one of four, reported three' reproduces that failure.

It existed to test the scope-boundary prediction; a profile settles that in minutes, attributes time WITHIN a run so it is immune to the cold/warm and machine-contention effects that made the sweep produce a confident wrong answer (a -39.5% q3 STOP that was a cold first run measured while an unrelated full gate ran), and it already answered the question: the four sites are 0.00%. Report inclusive percentages for the four sites, JoinLayout, and hashbrown. The four sites are expected to stay 0.00% on both sides — that IS the scope-boundary check, and a NON-zero reading is the STOP. (2) DELTA: extend tests/performance/unit/from_explicit_microbench.rs comparing an FxHashMap built from an ordered layout against the lazy ordered iterator, at 4 and 8 columns. RUN AS: cargo test --profile bench --no-default-features --test mod performance::unit::from_explicit_microbench -- --nocapture. Its own header documents '--test from_explicit_microbench', which is INVALID — the file is a module of the 'mod' target. Fix that stale header. The profile says these sites are unreached, so there is no workload in which to demonstrate one, and the microbench measures a constructor in isolation rather than a system effect. pack_join_results (select/join_dispatch.rs:369, col_order construction at :535-543) builds the emitted column order as the UNION across ALL rows, ordered by first occurrence (join_dispatch.rs:535-543: a col_order Vec guarded by a seen_cols FxHashSet, so later rows APPEND unseen columns). An earlier draft said it 'anchors on row 0 and normalises the rest to it' — equivalent only when every row shares one key set, not in general. The conclusion below survives the correction; the mechanism as previously stated did not. On the stream-STREAM path it unions rows from take-combine matched rows and site-933 NULL rows into one output_rows vec (join.rs:1264 and join.rs:1121,1317). Those two producers order columns DIFFERENTLY: take-combine goes through BuildSideStorage::new (hash_join.rs:162), which takes a RecordBatch, so its order is ARROW-SCHEMA derived; site 933 emits FxHashMap order. So the emitted schema ALREADY flips today between Arrow order (row 0 matched) and hash order (row 0 unmatched), and converting 933 to layout order plausibly REMOVES that flip rather than creating one. An earlier draft of this stop condition asserted the opposite — that the change creates a flip — and cited hash_join.rs:220 as evidence that take-combine is hash-ordered. That comment lives in BuildSideStorage::from_table_data, the stream-TABLE reference-snapshot path, which this path does not use. Do not go looking for hash order on the stream-stream take-combine side and conclude from its absence that there is no hazard. VERIFY the actual before-and-after order for both cases (row 0 matched, row 0 unmatched) before converting site 933. If after the change the two still differ, STOP and report: the scope boundary is wrong and that is an orchestrator decision, not something to patch around by widening the diff into hash_join.rs.

_depends_note: WAS blocked on #1919; UNBLOCKED 2026-09-16 when #2141 merged (0583961c8), and the re-derivation it demanded has now been DONE by the orchestrator — see _dedup_derivation. Keep reading that before touching sites 651/712/933.
_dedup_derivation: RESULT: layout.entries() names are UNIQUE on BOTH branches, BY CONSTRUCTION — independent of NB-005 and independent of the FxHashMap at the four sites. The dedup hazard (former stop condition 1) is REFUTED, so the map is NOT doing load-bearing dedup work and converting to a lazy iterator cannot change emitted cardinality. THE ARGUMENT: append_relation routes EVERY entry it adds — qualified AND bare — through shadow_or_append (layout.rs:299-318, 347-361), which dedups against name_pos. from_sides seeds a fresh name_pos and appends both relations that way (layout.rs:168-190). extend_with_right seeds name_pos FROM the left entries and appends the right the same way, so the right side can collide with neither the left nor itself. Hence entries can carry a duplicate ONLY IF the slice passed to from_existing_multi_source_fields already held one. That slice is left_record.data_field_names(), and the branch is taken only when those names are QUALIFIED — i.e. produced by a previous level of this same machinery, unique by the same argument. Induction closes. The pathological case, a source schema with a duplicated BARE column, takes from_sides instead, where shadow_or_append degrades to last-one-wins rather than emitting a literal duplicate — documented at layout.rs:342-346. WHAT THE EARLIER ANALYSIS GOT RIGHT AND WRONG: the observation that extend_with_right dedups only the right side and carries left duplicates through verbatim is CORRECT. The missing step was that left duplicates cannot exist. EMPIRICAL CONFIRMATION: multi_level_join_layout_emits_unique_qualified_names (multi_join_test.rs) drives a 3-way chain through QueryProcessor::process_query and reads data_field_names(), giving ['t.trade_id','t.user_id','t.amount','p.user_id','p.tier','k.discount_pct','k.tier'] — both join keys on both sides, tier on two relations, all qualified, zero duplicates. SELECT * is what makes this observable: a named projection renames everything to the SELECT list, and JoinLayout is private to the crate. A FIRST probe using a named projection measured the projection rather than the layout and would have 'confirmed' uniqueness while testing the wrong thing — do not repeat that. YOUR OBLIGATION: this is a derivation, not a licence. Confirm per site that the branch taken matches the above before removing each map, and if any site can reach from_existing with a non-layout-produced field list, STOP.
